en.name: Fresh pasta
en.summary: Fresh pasta is a refrigerated food, not a pantry one — soft dough, usually with egg in it, and often a filling of cheese or meat. It keeps 1–2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 2 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). Do not let dry pasta's two-year shelf life leak onto it.
en.pantry: Fresh pasta does not keep at room temperature. It has too much moisture in it to be stable, the egg makes it a richer growth medium than flour and water, and filled shapes contain cheese, ricotta or meat that are perishable in their own right. Leave it out no longer than the two-hour rule allows — one hour above 32 °C (90 °F) — and that includes the tray of ravioli you rolled and then went to answer the door.
en.fridge: Keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and cook it within 1–2 days. Shop-bought packs should stay sealed until you need them, and an unopened pack may carry a longer date because it was packed under modified atmosphere — once it is open, that date no longer means anything. Home-made pasta should go on a floured tray, well dusted and loosely covered so it does not sweat, and filled shapes should be kept in a single layer so they do not stick and tear. Cook filled pasta through, not just until the dough is done.
en.freezer: It keeps 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and freezing suits fresh pasta far better than a second day in the fridge. Freeze it on a floured tray first so the pieces stay separate, then bag them once solid and press the air out. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the two months are about quality, after which the dough goes brittle and filled shapes split on cooking.
en.thawing: Do not thaw fresh pasta — drop it straight from the freezer into plenty of boiling salted water and allow an extra minute or two. Thawed fresh pasta goes sticky and the filled shapes tear open.
spoilage: A sour or yeasty smell when the pack is opened.
A slimy or sticky surface, or dough that has gone tacky and grey.
Any mould spot, including at the sealed edge of a filled shape.
A pack that has puffed up or is leaking before it is opened.
tips: Freeze on the day of purchase anything you will not cook within a day or two.
Freeze on a floured tray first, then bag — otherwise you get one block.
Cook from frozen; thawing ruins the texture.
Do not confuse fresh pasta with dry pasta — their timelines have nothing in common.

faq.q: How long does fresh pasta keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. An unopened pack may carry a longer printed date, but once it is opened that no longer applies.
Yes, 2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze it spread out on a floured tray first, then bag it.

faq.q: Should you thaw frozen fresh pasta before cooking?
faq.a: No. Cook it straight from frozen in plenty of boiling water — thawed pasta goes sticky and filled shapes burst.

zh.name: 生鮮義大利麵
zh.summary: 生鮮義大利麵是冷藏食品，不是櫥櫃食品——柔軟的麵團，通常含蛋，很多還包著起司或肉餡。放 4 °C 以下冷藏 1～2 天，−18 °C 冷凍 2 個月。千萬不要把乾麵那個「兩年」的期限套到它身上。
zh.pantry: 生鮮義大利麵不能放常溫。它含水量太高、無法穩定，蛋又讓它比「麵粉加水」更適合微生物生長，而包餡款裡的起司、瑞可塔或肉本身就是易腐食品。離開冷藏不要超過 2 小時原則允許的時間，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時——包括你剛擀好一盤餃子、然後跑去應門的那段時間。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，1～2 天內煮掉。市售包裝要用之前都保持密封；未開封的包裝上可能印著更長的日期，那是因為充氣包裝的緣故——一旦拆封，那個日期就不再有意義。自製的請放在撒了粉的淺盤上，撲足手粉、鬆鬆地蓋著避免悶出水；包餡的要單層擺放，免得黏在一起一拿就破。包餡麵食要煮到「餡也熟」，不是麵皮熟就好。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下可放 2 個月，而且冷凍遠比「在冰箱多放一天」適合生鮮麵。先攤在撒粉的盤子上凍硬，讓每一個分開，再裝袋壓出空氣。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的；這兩個月講的是品質，之後麵皮會變脆，包餡款下鍋容易爆開。
zh.thawing: 生鮮義大利麵不要解凍——直接從冷凍丟進大量滾沸的鹽水，多煮一兩分鐘即可。解凍過的生麵會黏成一團，包餡的也會破。
spoilage: 拆封時聞到酸味或酵母味。
表面發黏，或麵團變得黏手、泛灰。
任何霉點，包括包餡麵食的封口處。
還沒開封就脹袋或滲液。
tips: 一兩天內煮不完的，買回來當天就冷凍。
先攤在撒粉的盤子上凍硬再裝袋，否則會結成一大塊。
直接從冷凍下鍋；解凍會毀掉口感。
不要把生鮮麵和乾麵混為一談——兩者的時程毫無關係。

faq.q: 生鮮義大利麵冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下 1～2 天。未開封包裝上可能印著更長的日期，但拆封後就不適用了。

faq.q: 生鮮義大利麵可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，−18 °C 下 2 個月。先攤在撒粉的盤子上凍硬再裝袋。

faq.q: 冷凍的生鮮義大利麵要先解凍嗎？
faq.a: 不要。直接從冷凍丟進大量滾水煮——解凍過會變黏，包餡的還會破掉。
